text: The KarstBinary 2025 prediction is dd504793-1ac3-4a1c-a389-707dbaab56c5 (completed). Fetching its results to get the result ID.

Result: result_id 419c581d-9a10-4684-aba5-1bab2875f26b, property sample_karst_score. In order to know the declared output range (to determine whether a threshold is needed for review_set_from_result), let me check the output of that property.

Since this band is a regression in [0,1], olmoearth_review_set_from_result can be used directly (it reads s as P(positive) for ranking). The window to check first is the one with a score closest to 0.5.

result.assumption: The band is a score in [0, 1] decided at 0.5 and is treated as P(positive) for ranking only: each window's scores are [1 - s, s], so its margin is |2s - 1| and the least decided windows (s nearest 0.5) are opened first; the most confident windows (s near 0 or 1) come last. Ranking by distance from 0.5 needs no calibration, but these numbers are not probabilities of error, and no recorded experiment grades this case.

sampling.what_a_window_is: a grid of sampled points, not every pixel: the result's extent is cut into 10 x 10 cells and each window is ONE pixel-value sample at its cell centre, so a window stands for its cell only as far as that pixel does
sampling.nodata_rule: a sample is no-data, and is dropped before ranking, when its band is missing or NaN, equals the model's nodata_value, lies outside the band's declared regression range, or carries no class on a classification band

result.signal: margin = distance from the decision (lower = more suspect, opened first); the most confident windows come last, never first

ceiling.note: No ranking can catch more than this share of the errors at a budget; judge a realised capture against it, not against 1.0. Pass error_rate (known or estimated) for the number.

result.listing_note: review lists all 7 windows of the review set at budget 0.1, in review order, so no list file is written; review_set_evidence.json (evidence_detail_path) holds evidence text only, no windows.

margin_summary.reading: Over all 72 windows: lowest_margin is the smallest margin (the most suspect window) and highest_margin the largest; median_margin is the middle value (half the windows lie below it), not a lower end. margin_at_budget_cut is the 7-th lowest margin (n_review at the budget); review_set is the margin range of all 7 windows in the review set, listed or not. The 65 windows ranked after the tool's 7 listed (ranks 8 to 72; not_listed) have margins from 0.785875 to 0.991517. These counts are the tool's listing's: a table of fewer than 7 rows leaves out more windows than not_listed counts, the extra ones with margins no higher than 0.785875.

result.evidence_scope: The ranking evidence (exp70 of 2imi9/olmoearth_inferenceX) was measured on OlmoEarth models' class-score margins and does not cover this case: no recorded experiment grades a regression score read as a probability.
caveats: Budgets are fractions of the valid sampled windows, not of the map's pixels.
This review set is chosen to hold errors; it is not a sample, and its error rate overstates the map's. To say how wrong the map is, use olmoearth_plan_label_sample.

facts.sentence: The median margin over all 72 windows (0.96469) is 1.30 to 3.25 times the margins of all 7 windows in the review set, every one listed (0.296909 to 0.744685).
Of the 7 windows in the review set, 4 (57.1%) are predicted class 0 (at or below the threshold 0.5) and 3 (42.9%) class 1 (above the threshold 0.5); every one of them is listed.

must_state: No recorded experiment grades a regression score read as a probability.

forbidden_claims.why: the margin orders windows for review; it is not a probability of error, and the review set is chosen to hold errors, not sampled, so no error rate follows from it without labelling a designed sample (olmoearth_plan_label_sample)

the margin orders windows for review, least decided first; it is not a probability of error, so no window of the review set is 'most likely wrong', 'probably an error' or 'likely mislabeled', and a low margin does not say a window is more likely wrong than right, nor, since no recorded experiment grades this ranking, are they 'the likeliest spots for a wrong call' or 'the windows most likely to be wrong': call them the least decided, the most suspect or the windows to check first; which of them are wrong is known only once they are labelled

evidence_scope names upstream evidence (exp70) that the tool says does not cover this case: none of its numbers, its dataset or its finding that the margin ranks errors well applies here, neither 'in comparable cases' nor as 'upstream evidence shows'; the file at evidence_detail_path keeps that record, not a finding about this case

result.next_step: To estimate how wrong this map is, pass scores_path to olmoearth_plan_label_sample (it chooses which windows to label); the file also holds each window's location for the reviewer.

content:
Checked the KarstBinary 2025 result (prediction `dd504793`, result `419c581d`) on a 10x10 grid: 72 valid windows, 28 no-data dropped. The band is a [0, 1] karst score decided at 0.5, so ranking opens the **least-decided windows first** — scores nearest 0.5 are most suspect.

**Check first (budget 10% = 7 windows):**

| Rank | Window (row, col) | Score | Margin | Predicted class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | (4, 7) | 0.352 | 0.297 | 0 |
| 2 | (4, 2) | 0.285 | 0.431 | 0 |
| 3 | (0, 5) | 0.745 | 0.490 | 1 |
| 4 | (1, 8) | 0.223 | 0.554 | 0 |
| 5 | (8, 5) | 0.808 | 0.615 | 1 |
| 6 | (2, 8) | 0.167 | 0.666 | 0 |
| 7 | (1, 3) | 0.872 | 0.745 | 1 |

**Why these:** each window's margin is its distance from the 0.5 decision — the model was least certain here, so this is where mislabeling risk concentrates. All 72 windows' median margin is 0.965, vs 0.30–0.74 for these. Scores were saved to `scores_419c581d..._g10.json` with locations for the reviewer.

Caveats: margin orders suspicion, it is **not** an error probability (no recorded experiment grades a regression score read this way), and this set is not a sample — its error rate would overstate the map's.

Next step, if you want: pass these scores to `olmoearth_plan_label_sample` to design an honest label budget for estimating how wrong the map actually is.
